Been an Age fan for years. The Definitive Edition Definitely brought a fresh breath into the game. Totally worth the investment, especially for an RTS lover. The Art of War Challenges decently prepare you for Competitive Multiplayer and the campaigns as well are well designed.

I played the original, of course. I like that the definitive edition gives a bit of polish to the game. It also is nice to have here on Steam so I can go for achievements and view my progress in one place. I don't remember there being this many civilizations last time around.

I definitely prefer playing random maps and going for a wonder victory. I know it's not a playstyle for everyone, but that's precisely what I love about the game. There's not *one way* to play the game. You can do historical things or fictional things; you can play with unique scenarios and imagine creative ways that civilizations may interact. The strategic balance is just right for me, providing enough challenge that you have to play seriously with it still being accessible enough that you can pick it up after a few weeks or months and remember how to play.

In short, it's a classic.

Lots of quality of life enhancements from the original games. Vastly graphically enhanced which also makes the game easier to play as it is easier to differentiate between textures and units. Dedicated servers vastly reduce the in game lag (they have had their issues which have been resolved for the most part).

Currently the biggest issue is stability. This is still being developed and hopefully the amount of crashes/disconnects will reduce.

New civs and new balance keep things interesting especially at a higher level. People played the same meta for over a decade so it's nice to see change .

It's a shame that mods are not done through the steam store and instead done in such a way that people who own the game on xbox can also use the mod center, it is rather bare bones compared to the workshop.

There have also been some issues with bugs introduced in DE that were not in the original, these for the most part have been resolved. Pathing still has some minor issues but nothing as bad as it was in the past.

If you enjoyed playing AOC back in the day I would certainly recommend playing DE. It's not perfect but it is certainly better than what we have had previously in terms of experience in its current state,

I had only ever played AOE1 and AOE3 back in the day. Thought I would go right in to AOE2 DE on hard difficulty, and boy was I in for a shock. The AI is much improved, and keeps you on your toes at all times. There are lots of achievements which took a while to get through, including one that involves multiplayer. But luckily everyone is really nice and helpful with it. There are some pathfinding issues which will be annoying at times and sometimes the game crashed randomly (due to soaking up memory). But overall it was fun and gets better as your skills improve.

I've been playing this game since the late 90s when it first came out. The professional tournament scene is alive and well, which is incredible for such an "old" game. It is very entertaining to watch tournaments and play online. Age of Empires is the game of ages!

Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition hits differently for me. This isn’t just a game I picked up recently it’s something I’ve been playing since childhood. I still remember sitting in my dad’s shop playing alongside my older sibling, figuring out strategies, arguing over decisions, and enjoying every moment of it.

Coming back to it now in the Definitive Edition feels like reliving those memories, but upgraded in every way. The graphics are cleaner, the sound design is better, and there’s so much more content but somehow it still feels exactly like the same game I grew up with.

The strategy depth is what really keeps it alive. Every match forces you to think whether you’re rushing early, building a strong economy, or setting up for late-game domination. No two games ever feel the same.

What I respect the most is how they improved everything without ruining the core experience. It still has that classic feel, just smoother and more polished.

Honestly, this game isn’t just about winning or losing it’s about the memories, the strategy, and those intense matches that keep you coming back.

Timeless classic. Always will be.

I have played this game since I was young, way before Steam's inception. As a real time strategy game, this is definitely my favorite. With that being said, this game does require a bit of a learning curve to master (like most RTS games). Even for me, a veteran at this game, it took me multiple big L's before slowly learning and understanding what I should be doing. And this is just playing the single player campaign mode against hard AI. I know that it is much more competitive in playing against others. Everything needs to be done perfectly. Leaving the town center idle for half a second could have a huge butterfly effect later. In summary, if you are not trying to be competitive, you can enjoy this game in campaign mode, which are challenging but mostly fair. If you are competitive, playing against other players in this game is definitely for you.
